comment: HealthAgentBench v2: 75 tasks in nine categories. Frozen v1 metadata remains in tasks.json.

families.title: X-ray Report Correction
families.blurb: Review a chest X-ray Findings draft against the target study and longitudinal history, then write the corrected report section. Success requires a majority of judges to find no significant errors.

families.title: CT Abnormality Classification
families.blurb: Interpret a chest CT volume and emit a per-volume yes/no label vector for the report-grounded abnormality findings. Success criteria: 1.0 accuracy.

families.title: Pathology Tumor Area Selection
families.blurb: Inspect a gigapixel pathology slide and predict the set of tumor tiles on a fixed analysis grid. Success criteria: ≥ 0.9 tile F1.

families.title: Pathology Tumor Slide Selection
families.blurb: Inspect eight whole-slide H&E images and identify every slide containing malignant tumor cells. Success requires an exact match to the tumor-slide set, including empty sets.

families.title: MRI QA
families.blurb: Review three MRI examinations from the supplied axial, coronal, and sagittal arrays. Answer ACL-tear and meniscal-tear questions for each exam. All six answers must match the source labels.

families.title: EHR Data Quality Auditing
families.blurb: Audit an EHR corpus containing injected errors and flag affected rows. Success requires error-cluster recall of 1.0 and row-level precision of at least 0.1.

families.title: EHR Compositional QA
families.blurb: Answer numerical clinical questions from raw MIMIC-IV tables, using 1,020 labeled examples to validate calculations. Five question-category tasks and one combined task require every answer correct.

families.title: EHR Event Modelling
families.blurb: Learn from labeled longitudinal EHR timelines and predict held-out clinical-event risks using only observable history. Success requires AUROC to match or exceed the reference baseline.

families.title: Cancer Survival Prediction
families.blurb: Predict overall survival time for five cancer cohorts using labeled training data. Success requires full prediction coverage and better C-index, censoring-adjusted error, and integrated Brier score than both Cox and RSF baselines.
